subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The major 1536 rebellion in the north against religious change and Cromwell was called the:
questions.explain: The Pilgrimage of Grace (1536), led by Robert Aske, was the most serious rebellion against the Henrician Reformation.

questions.q: Henry VII's eldest son and heir, who died in 1502, was named:
questions.explain: Prince Arthur died in 1502 shortly after marrying Catherine of Aragon, making his brother Henry the heir to the throne.

questions.q: Elizabeth I's chief minister for most of her reign, created Lord Burghley, was:
questions.explain: William Cecil, Lord Burghley, was Elizabeth's principal Secretary and then Lord Treasurer, the cornerstone of her government.

questions.q: Elizabeth I's religious settlement was established by which two 1559 statutes?
options: The Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity
The Acts of Appeals and Annates
The Acts of Six and Ten Articles
The Acts of Succession and Treason
questions.explain: The 1559 Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity created the Elizabethan Church settlement, making Elizabeth Supreme Governor.

questions.q: In which year did the Spanish Armada attempt to invade England?
questions.explain: The Spanish Armada sailed in 1588 and was defeated by the English fleet and storms, a defining moment of Elizabeth's reign.

questions.q: Who commanded the Spanish Armada of 1588?
questions.explain: The Duke of Medina Sidonia commanded the Armada in 1588, intending to link with Parma's army in the Netherlands.

questions.q: During Edward VI's minority, who served as Lord Protector from 1547 until his fall in 1549?
questions.explain: Edward Seymour, Duke of Somerset, was Lord Protector until political failure and Kett's Rebellion led to his removal in 1549.

questions.q: The 1549 rebellion in Norfolk led by a tanner protesting against enclosure was:
questions.explain: Kett's Rebellion (1549) in East Anglia protested against enclosure and rural grievances during Edward VI's reign.

questions.q: The Dissolution of the smaller monasteries began with which 1536 statute?
options: The Act for the Dissolution of the Lesser Monasteries
questions.explain: The 1536 Act dissolved smaller monasteries (under 200 pounds annual income), beginning the seizure of monastic wealth.

questions.q: England lost its last continental possession during Mary I's reign in 1558, namely:
questions.explain: Calais, held since 1347, fell to French forces in January 1558, a humiliating loss late in Mary I's reign.

questions.q: At which battle in 1485 did Henry Tudor defeat Richard III to seize the English throne?
questions.explain: Henry Tudor defeated and killed Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field on 22 August 1485, founding the Tudor dynasty.

questions.q: The first English Book of Common Prayer, imposed by an Act of Uniformity, appeared in which year?
questions.explain: Cranmer's first Book of Common Prayer was introduced in 1549, a more radical revision following in 1552.

questions.q: Which 1487 battle saw Henry VII defeat the Yorkist pretender Lambert Simnel's forces?
questions.explain: The Battle of Stoke Field in June 1487 crushed the rebellion backing Lambert Simnel, who was then put to work in the royal kitchens.

questions.q: Which two financial agents became notorious for Henry VII's harsh use of bonds and recognisances?
questions.explain: Edmund Dudley and Richard Empson administered Henry VII's exploitative financial policies and were executed under Henry VIII in 1510.

questions.q: The Treaty of Etaples (1492) committed France to which key concession to Henry VII?
options: Withdrawing support from Perkin Warbeck and paying a pension
questions.explain: By the Treaty of Etaples, France agreed to stop backing Warbeck and to pay Henry an annual pension, securing his throne and finances.

questions.q: The lavish 1520 diplomatic summit between Henry VIII and Francis I of France is known as the:
options: Field of the Cloth of Gold
questions.explain: The Field of the Cloth of Gold (1520) was an extravagant meeting near Calais designed to display Anglo-French amity, organised by Wolsey.

questions.q: Elizabeth I's famous speech rallying troops against the Armada was delivered at which location in 1588?
questions.explain: Elizabeth delivered her stirring speech to the troops at Tilbury in August 1588 during the Armada crisis.

questions.q: Which of Henry VIII's wives was the mother of the future Edward VI?
questions.explain: Jane Seymour bore Henry's only legitimate son, the future Edward VI, in 1537, dying days later.

questions.q: Which 1570 papal bull excommunicated Elizabeth I and released her subjects from allegiance?
questions.explain: Pope Pius V issued Regnans in Excelsis in 1570, excommunicating Elizabeth and intensifying the Catholic threat.

questions.q: In which year was Mary, Queen of Scots executed at Fotheringhay Castle?
questions.explain: Mary, Queen of Scots was executed in February 1587 after being convicted of complicity in the Babington Plot.

questions.q: Henry VII dated the start of his reign to the day before Bosworth so that he could attaint which group as traitors?
options: Those who fought for Richard III
questions.explain: By backdating his reign to 21 August 1485 he could treat Richard III's supporters at Bosworth as traitors and pass acts of attainder against them.

questions.q: Wolsey fell from power in 1529 chiefly because of his failure to secure what for Henry VIII?
options: An annulment of the marriage to Catherine of Aragon
questions.explain: Wolsey's inability to obtain papal annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon led to his disgrace in 1529.

questions.q: Who did John Dudley, Duke of Northumberland, attempt to place on the throne after Edward VI's death in 1553?
questions.explain: Northumberland tried to put his daughter-in-law Lady Jane Grey on the throne in July 1553, but Mary Tudor swiftly prevailed.

questions.q: In which year was the Act of Supremacy passed, making Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England?
questions.explain: The Act of Supremacy of 1534 declared Henry VIII the Supreme Head of the Church of England, completing the break with Rome.

questions.q: The 1569 rebellion of the Catholic earls of Northumberland and Westmorland is known as the:
questions.explain: The Rising of the North (1569) sought to free Mary, Queen of Scots and restore Catholicism, but was swiftly crushed.

questions.q: In what year did Henry VIII accede to the throne following his father's death?
questions.explain: Henry VII died in April 1509 and Henry VIII succeeded, soon marrying Catherine of Aragon, his brother's widow.

questions.q: Which two leading Protestant bishops were burned at Oxford in 1555 during the Marian persecutions?
questions.explain: Hugh Latimer and Nicholas Ridley were burned at Oxford in 1555; Cranmer followed in 1556 during Mary I's restoration of Catholicism.

questions.q: Sir Thomas More was executed in 1535 for refusing to swear which oath?
options: The Oath of Succession and Supremacy
questions.explain: More refused to acknowledge the royal supremacy and Anne Boleyn's succession, and was executed for treason in July 1535.

questions.q: The 1586 plot to assassinate Elizabeth and free Mary, Queen of Scots, uncovered by Walsingham, was the:
questions.explain: The Babington Plot of 1586 implicated Mary in a plan to kill Elizabeth, leading directly to Mary's trial and execution.

questions.q: Thomas Wolsey rose to dominate government after which 1513 military campaign in France that he organised?
options: The Battle of the Spurs campaign
questions.explain: Wolsey's effective organisation of the 1513 French campaign, including the Battle of the Spurs, secured Henry VIII's favour and his rise.
